articles.title: Windows 11 24H2 Support Has Ended: What to Do Now and How to Upgrade Safely
articles.subtitle: What Windows 11 24H2 end of support means for your device, how to check your current build, and step-by-step instructions to upgrade safely.
articles.excerpt: Everything you need to know about Windows 11 24H2 reaching end of servicing: security risks, compatibility checks, and how to upgrade safely without losing files.
articles.metaTitle: Windows 11 24H2 Support Has Ended: What to Do Now and How to Upgrade Safely | Zee Writes
articles.metaDescription: Windows 11 24H2 support has ended. Follow this step-by-step guide to verify your build, backup your files, and upgrade safely to the latest supported release.

coverImage.alt: Windows 11 24H2 Upgrade and Security Servicing Lifecycle Guide
coverImage.caption: Step-by-step Windows 11 servicing lifecycle and safe in-place upgrade path.

verifiedTakeaway.symptom: Windows Update displays 'Your device is nearing the end of service' or stops receiving monthly cumulative security patches.
verifiedTakeaway.rootCause: Microsoft enforces servicing timelines for Windows 11 feature updates. When a build reaches its retirement date, cumulative security updates and technical assistance cease.
verifiedTakeaway.instantFix: Verify hardware compatibility, create a system restore point, and run the official Windows Update Assistant or in-place upgrade.

howToSteps.name: Check Your Current Windows 11 Build
howToSteps.text: Press Windows Key + R, type winver in the Run dialog, and press Enter. Confirm whether your version reads Version 24H2 and note your OS Build number.
howToSteps.proTip: You can also open PowerShell and run: Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion' | Select-Object DisplayVersion, CurrentBuild

howToSteps.name: Create a System Restore Point & Backup
howToSteps.text: Before upgrading, ensure your important files are backed up to an external drive or cloud storage. Open Create a restore point from the Start menu and click Create.
howToSteps.proTip: Having a recent restore point ensures you can roll back within 10 days if any third-party driver conflicts occur.

howToSteps.name: Trigger the Official Upgrade via Windows Update
howToSteps.text: Navigate to Settings > Windows Update and click Check for updates. If the next feature update is ready for your hardware, click Download & install.
howToSteps.proTip: Ensure you have at least 20 GB of free drive space on your C: drive before starting the installation.

howToSteps.name: Verify Installation and Enable Secure Baseline
howToSteps.text: After the system restarts and finishes the upgrade, open Settings > System > About to confirm your new Windows version and verify that Windows Security shows all green checks.

sections.heading: 1. What Does Windows 11 24H2 End of Support Mean?
paragraphs: When a Windows 11 version reaches its End of Servicing date, Microsoft no longer provides monthly security intelligence updates, bug fixes, or technical support for that specific build.

While your PC will continue to boot and run installed applications normally, it becomes progressively more vulnerable to newly discovered zero-day exploits and malware that target unpatched kernel vulnerabilities.

callout.title: Security Warning
callout.body: Running an unserviced operating system on a network exposes your local credentials, browser sessions, and stored data to unpatched remote-code execution vulnerabilities.

sections.heading: 2. Recommended Action Plan for Users
paragraphs: The safest and most reliable course of action is to perform an in-place upgrade to the latest supported Windows 11 feature update. In-place upgrades preserve all your personal files, desktop settings, and installed applications while replacing the core system files with the latest secure build.
Ensure your device meets the standard Windows 11 hardware baseline: TPM 2.0 enabled in UEFI BIOS, Secure Boot active, and at least 64 GB of total system storage.

sections.heading: 3. Troubleshooting Common Upgrade Blockers
paragraphs: If Windows Update fails with error codes such as 0x80070070 (insufficient disk space) or 0xC1900101 (driver conflict), run the built-in Windows Update Troubleshooter and temporarily disconnect external USB peripherals.
You can reset the Windows Update cache by stopping the update services, clearing the SoftwareDistribution folder, and restarting the service.

codeBlock.code:
net stop wuauserv
net stop cryptSvc
net stop bits
ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
net start wuauserv
net start cryptSvc
net start bits

faqs.question: Will my computer stop working after Windows 11 24H2 support ends?
faqs.answer: No, your computer will not suddenly shut down or stop functioning. However, it will no longer receive monthly cumulative security patches from Microsoft, leaving it vulnerable to new security threats.

faqs.question: Is upgrading to the next supported Windows 11 release free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feature updates for Windows 11 are completely free for all licensed Windows 11 users through Windows Update.

faqs.question: Will upgrading delete my files, games, or applications?
faqs.answer: A standard in-place update through Windows Update or the official Update Assistant retains all of your personal files, desktop icons, browser bookmarks, and installed software.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Quick Answer A good prompt tells the AI five things: who it should act as, what you want, the background, what the answer should look like, and what limits to follow. The clearer you are, the better the answer. If the first answer isn’t good, don’t start over. Reply with what to change. This works the same way in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. Why most prompts fail Vague in, vague out. A prompt like “Write about smartphones” could mean a thousand things. The AI fills the gaps with guesses, and guesses sound generic. The fix is to say what you actually want. The 5-part prompt Write it like a message to a smart new assistant who knows nothing about your situation. 1. Role: Who should the AI act as? Example: “You are a patient math tutor.” 2. Task: What exactly should it do? Example: “Explain how to add fractions.” 3. Context: What does it need to know? Example: “I’m 14 and I get stuck when the bottom numbers are different.” 4. Format: What should the answer look like? Example: “Five steps, short sentences, one example for each step.” 5. Limits: What should it avoid or keep? Example: “Under 200 words. No jargon.” Here is the difference it makes. Weak prompt: Write about smartphones. Better prompt: You are a tech writer. Write a 150-word buying tip for first-time smartphone buyers with a budget under $300. Use simple words and end with one question they should ask the shop assistant. You don’t need all five parts every time. For a quick question, a clear task is enough. For anything you will use or publish, add the rest. 8 habits that improve any prompt 1. Name the audience. “For a 10-year-old” and “for a doctor” give very different answers. 2. Say the length. “In 100 words” or “in 5 bullets.” 3. Show an example. Paste a sample of what you like and say “write in this style.” 4. Paste your own material. Add the text, the numbers or the error message, and say “use only this.” 5. Let it ask you questions. For bigger jobs, add: “Ask me up to five questions before you start.” 6. Break big jobs into steps. Do the outline first, then each section. 7. Say what to avoid. For example: “No hype words. No long intro.” 8. Reply to improve. “Make it shorter.” “Make it more casual.” “Show it as a table.” 15 copy-paste prompts Replace anything in [brackets] with your own details. Study 1. Explain a topic from zero: Explain [topic] to me as if I’m a complete beginner. Use one simple everyday example, then give me 3 questions to test myself. Keep it under 250 words. 2. Build a study plan: I have [number] days to learn [subject] for an exam. I can study [number] hours a day. Make a day-by-day plan with short goals, and tell me what to review on the last day. 3. Quiz me: Quiz me on [topic], one question at a time. Wait for my answer, tell me if it’s right, explain briefly, then ask the next one. Start easy and get harder. Work 4. Write an email: Write a short, polite email to [person or role] about [topic]. My goal is [goal]. Tone: friendly but professional. Under 120 words. Give me two subject line options. 5. Summarize a long text: Summarize the text below in 5 bullet points for a busy manager. Then list any dates, numbers and action items. Text: [paste text] 6. Clean up meeting notes: Turn these rough notes into clean meeting minutes with three parts: decisions, action items with owners, and open questions. Notes: [paste notes] 7. Improve a CV for a job: Below are a job description and my CV. Tell me the 5 skills I should highlight, and suggest one stronger bullet point for each. Don’t invent experience I don’t have. Job: [paste] CV: [paste] Writing 8. Plan a blog post: Create an outline for a blog post called [title] for [audience]. Give me a short intro idea, 5 section headings, and 2 points under each heading. Use simple words. 9. Edit my draft: Edit the text below for clarity. Fix grammar, cut filler words, and keep my voice. After the edited version, list the main changes you made. Text: [paste text] 10. Make it shorter: Cut this text to half its length. Keep the main point and every number. Text: [paste text] Tech help 11. Fix an error: I’m getting this error on [device or software and version]: [paste error]. Explain what it means in simple words. Then give me fixes to try, from easiest to hardest, and tell me what to check after each one. 12. Explain code: Explain what this code does, line by line, for a beginner. Then point out any bug or risky part. Code: [paste code] 13. Get a spreadsheet formula: I use [Excel or Google Sheets]. My data is in columns A to D: [describe the columns]. I want to [goal]. Give me the formula and explain how it works. Daily life 14. Compare two options: Compare [option A] and [option B] for someone who [your situation]. Use a table with price, pros, cons and who each one suits. Tell me which one you would pick, why, and what you’re unsure about. 15. Plan a trip, event or week: Help me plan [trip, event or week]. I have [budget or time]. I like [things] and want to avoid [things]. Give me a simple plan. If you need more details, ask me 3 questions first. Phrases to improve any answer Keep these ready for your second message: • “Make it shorter.” • “Use simpler words.” • “Give me three different versions.” • “List the assumptions you made.” • “What could be wrong with this answer?” • “Show that as a table.” • “Explain step 3 in more detail.” Mistakes to avoid • Pasting private data. Don’t put passwords, ID numbers, bank details or client secrets into a chat tool. • Trusting facts without checking. AI can sound sure and be wrong. It can also make up numbers, quotes and links. Check anything that matters. • Asking for ten things at once. Split big requests into steps. • Treating the first answer as final. Reply and push it in the right direction. • Publishing AI text as it is. Edit it so it sounds like you, add your own examples, and follow the rules of your school or workplace about AI use. Do prompts work differently in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini? The basics are the same in all of them. Each tool has its own style, so if one answer is weak, try the same prompt in another tool or add more detail. Keep the version that works best for you. FAQ Do I need to learn “prompt engineering”? For most people, no. Clear writing is enough. Say what you want, who it’s for, and what the answer should look like. Are longer prompts always better? No. Clear beats long. Add details that change the answer, and skip the rest. Can the AI remember my earlier chats? It depends on the tool and your settings. Check the settings before you share personal details. Are these tools free? Most have a free plan with limits. The limits change often, so check each tool’s own page.

articles.rawMarkdown:
Quick Answer
A good prompt tells the AI five things: who it should act as, what you want, the background, what the answer should look like, and what limits to follow. The clearer you are, the better the answer. If the first answer isn’t good, don’t start over. Reply with what to change. This works the same way in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.
Why most prompts fail
Vague in, vague out. A prompt like “Write about smartphones” could mean a thousand things. The AI fills the gaps with guesses, and guesses sound generic. The fix is to say what you actually want.
The 5-part prompt
Write it like a message to a smart new assistant who knows nothing about your situation.
1. Role: Who should the AI act as? Example: “You are a patient math tutor.”
2. Task: What exactly should it do? Example: “Explain how to add fractions.”
3. Context: What does it need to know? Example: “I’m 14 and I get stuck when the bottom numbers are different.”
4. Format: What should the answer look like? Example: “Five steps, short sentences, one example for each step.”
5. Limits: What should it avoid or keep? Example: “Under 200 words. No jargon.”
Here is the difference it makes.
Weak prompt:
Write about smartphones.
Better prompt:
You are a tech writer. Write a 150-word buying tip for first-time smartphone buyers with a budget under $300. Use simple words and end with one question they should ask the shop assistant.
You don’t need all five parts every time. For a quick question, a clear task is enough. For anything you will use or publish, add the rest.
8 habits that improve any prompt
1. Name the audience. “For a 10-year-old” and “for a doctor” give very different answers.
2. Say the length. “In 100 words” or “in 5 bullets.”
3. Show an example. Paste a sample of what you like and say “write in this style.”
4. Paste your own material. Add the text, the numbers or the error message, and say “use only this.”
5. Let it ask you questions. For bigger jobs, add: “Ask me up to five questions before you start.”
6. Break big jobs into steps. Do the outline first, then each section.
7. Say what to avoid. For example: “No hype words. No long intro.”
8. Reply to improve. “Make it shorter.” “Make it more casual.” “Show it as a table.”
15 copy-paste prompts
Replace anything in [brackets] with your own details.
Study
1. Explain a topic from zero:
Explain [topic] to me as if I’m a complete beginner. Use one simple everyday example, then give me 3 questions to test myself. Keep it under 250 words.
2. Build a study plan:
I have [number] days to learn [subject] for an exam. I can study [number] hours a day. Make a day-by-day plan with short goals, and tell me what to review on the last day.
3. Quiz me:
Quiz me on [topic], one question at a time. Wait for my answer, tell me if it’s right, explain briefly, then ask the next one. Start easy and get harder.
Work
4. Write an email:
Write a short, polite email to [person or role] about [topic]. My goal is [goal]. Tone: friendly but professional. Under 120 words. Give me two subject line options.
5. Summarize a long text:
Summarize the text below in 5 bullet points for a busy manager. Then list any dates, numbers and action items. Text: [paste text]
6. Clean up meeting notes:
Turn these rough notes into clean meeting minutes with three parts: decisions, action items with owners, and open questions. Notes: [paste notes]
7. Improve a CV for a job:
Below are a job description and my CV. Tell me the 5 skills I should highlight, and suggest one stronger bullet point for each. Don’t invent experience I don’t have. Job: [paste] CV: [paste]
Writing
8. Plan a blog post:
Create an outline for a blog post called [title] for [audience]. Give me a short intro idea, 5 section headings, and 2 points under each heading. Use simple words.
9. Edit my draft:
Edit the text below for clarity. Fix grammar, cut filler words, and keep my voice. After the edited version, list the main changes you made. Text: [paste text]
10. Make it shorter:
Cut this text to half its length. Keep the main point and every number. Text: [paste text]
Tech help
11. Fix an error:
I’m getting this error on [device or software and version]: [paste error]. Explain what it means in simple words. Then give me fixes to try, from easiest to hardest, and tell me what to check after each one.
12. Explain code:
Explain what this code does, line by line, for a beginner. Then point out any bug or risky part. Code: [paste code]
13. Get a spreadsheet formula:
I use [Excel or Google Sheets]. My data is in columns A to D: [describe the columns]. I want to [goal]. Give me the formula and explain how it works.
Daily life
14. Compare two options:
Compare [option A] and [option B] for someone who [your situation]. Use a table with price, pros, cons and who each one suits. Tell me which one you would pick, why, and what you’re unsure about.
15. Plan a trip, event or week:
Help me plan [trip, event or week]. I have [budget or time]. I like [things] and want to avoid [things]. Give me a simple plan. If you need more details, ask me 3 questions first.
Phrases to improve any answer
Keep these ready for your second message:
• “Make it shorter.”
• “Use simpler words.”
• “Give me three different versions.”
• “List the assumptions you made.”
• “What could be wrong with this answer?”
• “Show that as a table.”
• “Explain step 3 in more detail.”
Mistakes to avoid
• Pasting private data. Don’t put passwords, ID numbers, bank details or client secrets into a chat tool.
• Trusting facts without checking. AI can sound sure and be wrong. It can also make up numbers, quotes and links. Check anything that matters.
• Asking for ten things at once. Split big requests into steps.
• Treating the first answer as final. Reply and push it in the right direction.
• Publishing AI text as it is. Edit it so it sounds like you, add your own examples, and follow the rules of your school or workplace about AI use.
Do prompts work differently in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini?
The basics are the same in all of them. Each tool has its own style, so if one answer is weak, try the same prompt in another tool or add more detail. Keep the version that works best for you.
FAQ
Do I need to learn “prompt engineering”? For most people, no. Clear writing is enough. Say what you want, who it’s for, and what the answer should look like.
Are longer prompts always better? No. Clear beats long. Add details that change the answer, and skip the rest.
Can the AI remember my earlier chats? It depends on the tool and your settings. Check the settings before you share personal details.
Are these tools free? Most have a free plan with limits. The limits change often, so check each tool’s own page.
